In [[mathematics]], <!-- especially in the area of MAJOR FIELD, known as MINOR FIELD --> a '''paratopological group''' is a [[topological semigroup]] that is algebraically a [[group (mathematics)|group]].<ref>Artur Hideyuki Tomita. [https://tatra.mat.savba.sk/Full/14/10tomita.ps On sequentially compact both-sides cancellative semigroups with sequentially continuous addition.]</ref> In other words, it is a group ''G'' with a topology such that the group's product operation is a [[continuous function]] from ''G''&nbsp;×&nbsp;''G'' to ''G''. This differs from the definition of a [[topological group]] in that the group inverse is not required to be continuous.

As with topological groups, some authors require the topology to be [[Hausdorff space|Hausdorff]].<ref>[[Alexander Arhangelskii|A. V. Arhangelskii]]. [http://atlas-conferences.com/c/a/v/h/18.htm Topological spaces connected to algebraic structures] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110608074634/http://atlas-conferences.com/c/a/v/h/18.htm |date=2011-06-08 }}</ref>

[[compact space|Compact]] paratopological groups are automatically topological groups.
